title: Dedicated cluster post-incident: allocator tuning, noisy-neighbor attribution, and burst smoothing
creator: Priya Nair
description: Summary: A dedicated-cluster capacity event led to elevated evictions and degraded tail latency for multiple tenants during a traffic surge on 2026-02-09. Root cause analysis shows a confluence of (1) an unexpectedly noisy tenant with sustained KV/prefix cache pressure, (2) reservation mis-sizing for a subset of pools (under-provisioned headroom), and (3) burst token logic that allowed short-term oversubscription without adequate backoff. The incident surfaced limits in our allocator heuristics and insufficient attribution telemetry to quickly identify the noisy workload. This ticket tracks the post-incident action items: allocator tuning, noisy-neighbor attribution, reservation reconciliation, burst smoothing, and improved alerting/playbooks.
action_items: Add tenant-level GPU/CPU and token-burn attribution metrics to the allocator stream; emit per-tenant 1m/5m burn-rate (owner: Ben Carter) — ETA 2w
Build periodic reservation-reconciliation job that compares actual 95th usage to reserved capacity and flags candidates for rightsizing suggestions (owner: Priya Nair) — ETA 3w
Prototype burst-smoothing algorithm: apply exponential backoff to burst tokens and gradual refill to prevent short spikes from saturating pools (owner: Asha Kapoor) — ETA 2w
Add eviction-protection SLO: if per-node eviction rate > threshold, throttle new burst grants and scale alternative capacity (owner: Miguel Alvarez) — ETA 1w
Create Grafana dashboard and run-book panels for 'burst grants vs steady-state tokens' and 'per-tenant eviction attribution' (owner: SRE) — ETA 4d
Instrument end-to-end integration tests that simulate noisy-tenant pattern and verify allocator defends other tenants (owner: infra-tests) — ETA 2w
Update Dedicated runbook and oncall play for capacity events with step-by-step tenant isolation and suggested mitigation commands (owner: Product Ops) — ETA 1w
decisions: Retain soft-burst capability but introduce a 10s rate cap and exponential backoff per tenant once a 30s sustained burn threshold is crossed
Do not enable automatic permanent reservation resizing without human approval; instead surface suggested rightsizes in Console with a one-click approve flow
Authorize periodic (daily) reservation reconciliation audits for pools with >15% sustained variance between reserved and 95th usage
Add a dedicated 'noisy-tenant' tag and short-lived eviction quarantine to prevent noisy workloads from repeatedly being scheduled to the same node group
timeline: 2026-02-09 08:14 UTC — Oncall triggered by spike in evictions for dedicated-cluster-east-1; initial mitigation: increased burst limits for burst-eligible pools to prevent immediate request failures
2026-02-09 08:25 UTC — Identification of tenant 'svc-analytics-7' as top token burner via slow logs; mitigations started: rebalance traffic and pin tenant to lower-priority pool
2026-02-09 09:00 UTC — Eviction spike reduced but tail latency still elevated; triage meeting convened (Infra, SRE, Product) and postmortem timeline captured

2026-02-10 — Root cause analysis: reservation under-provisioning in several pools (some reservations based on outdated telemetry), and burst tokens permitted short-term oversubscription during sustained bursts
2026-02-12 — Temporary guard deployed: burst grant window reduced from 60s to 30s and a per-tenant cap applied. Incident declared mitigated. Draft action items assigned.
blockers: Need node-pool autoscaler permission update from Cloud infra before automating reservation resize on prod (pending security review)
Some test harness gaps in simulator for long-running KV cache behavior — infra-tests needs 2d of work
followups: Run a 4-week telemetry collection period after burst-smoothing rollout to validate tail latency and per-tenant isolation improvements
Schedule a cross-team RFC to standardize reservation sizing heuristics: include Product, Runtime, SRE, and Sales (to capture enterprise reserved-contract constraints)
Add an automated weekly report for pools with >10% variance between reserved capacity and 95th usage and notify owners
Plan a chaos test that emulates noisy-tenant memory/KV pressure to validate isolation and eviction protections (owner: Reliability)
